nodes.text: We are glad you are here
Who we are, how we work, your first thirty days, the people to meet, and where to ask anything.
Your first week, with the People team  ·  November 2026
Every community organisation should run on tools as good as any company's. We build them, and we keep them affordable.
Subscriptions from organisations over fifty people. Everything under that is free, and always will be.
One hundred and twelve people in three offices and eleven countries. Most of us work from home two days a week.
the free tier is the point, not the funnel
Three rituals, three tools, three rules.
Thirty minutes, the whole team, what matters this week.
Anyone shows anything that shipped. Fifteen minutes, no slides.
What went well, what did not, one thing to change.
Public channels by default. DMs for the personal stuff.
If it is not written down there, it was not decided.
Every task has an owner and a week. Nothing lives in a chat.
Someone else has the same question. Channels, not DMs.
Comments first, then the meeting decides, then we commit.
In the channel, in the retro, in the all-hands.
not written down? ask, then write it down
A week to look around, a week to shadow, a week to own something small, and a chat about what comes next.
Nothing to prepare. Turn up at nine with your ID, and we take it from there.
Your badge and your buddy are waiting
Sign in with the email we sent last week
By the window, with your team
Lunch at half twelve, all of us
The long table by the kitchen
leave at four, we mean it
thirteen stops, no deliverables, lots of questions
Your buddy, your team, your manager. The wiki's welcome page, end to end. No deliverables.
Sit with support for a day and with a customer call. Ship one small change, with help.
A ticket, a doc, a customer question. Yours start to finish.
A thirty-minute chat with your manager: what surprised you, what is unclear, what you want next.
week four is a chat, not a review
Books a coffee with every new hire in the first month. Take her up on it.
Your first stop for anything about pay, leave, equipment or how things work.
Runs the Wednesday demo. Ask him for the architecture tour.
Knows what customers actually ask. Shadow her team in week two.
all four have already said yes to a coffee
No silly questions in your first month, and very few after that. Your buddy, the People channel, or anyone in the kitchen.
Your week-four chat is already booked
the kitchen counts as a channel
